reason: This text fragment (1 Samuel 17) depicts the confrontation between David and Goliath. While the Israelites are indeed suffering and greatly afraid ('וַיֵּחַתּוּ וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מְאֹֽד' - 'they were dismayed and greatly afraid'), no leader tells them their suffering is their own fault. The only rebuke is Eliab's personal criticism of David for leaving his sheep to come to the battle, not a leader blaming the people collectively for their predicament. Saul actually encourages David by saying 'Let not the heart of a man fall upon him.' The passage shows fear and discouragement but no instance of leaders attributing the suffering to the people's failings.
